dataset_source: Sentinel-1 Typical Oceanic and Atmospheric Phenomena Semantic Segmentation Dataset (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.14279466)

governance_invariants.hm_naming_rule: Class 13 (HM) must be named Artificial / Anthropogenic Objects; renaming to Vessel is strictly forbidden.
governance_invariants.os_exclusion_rule: Class 14 (OS) is known to have only 4 images (1,702 pixels, 0.0005% of dataset) and is explicitly flagged as insufficient data; it is strictly excluded from OPS-01 training.
governance_invariants.lookalike_attribution_rule: Li classes are candidate look-alikes; specific causal attribution to EXP-06 false alarms remains an unproven engineering hypothesis requiring validation.

classes.semantic_definition: Ambient open-ocean sea surface without discrete identifiable meteorological or hydrodynamic phenomena. Formed by unannotated marine matrix in source annotations.
classes.known_ambiguities: Low backscatter regions under gentle breezes may visually transition into biogenic films or low wind areas.

classes.semantic_definition: Synoptic or mesoscale air-mass boundary causing sharp spatial gradients in near-surface wind speed, visible as sharp brightness steps or linear shear zones.
classes.known_ambiguities: Frontal sharp edges can be confused with gust fronts or current shear boundaries.

classes.semantic_definition: Natural monomolecular surfactant films derived from marine plankton, phytoplankton blooms, or fish oils that damp short capillary-gravity waves via the Marangoni effect.
classes.known_ambiguities: Primary look-alike to mineral oil spills. Distinguishable in multi-modal/context by lack of point-source discharge, diffuse dendritic morphology, and coincidence with chlorophyll/productivity zones.

classes.semantic_definition: Discrete floating glacial ice fragments or clusters detached from ice shelves or glaciers, presenting high backscatter targets in polar waters.
classes.exclusion_reason: Domain-restricted cryospheric hazard; low relevance to temperate/tropical oil-spill monitoring; reserved for specialized polar models.
classes.known_ambiguities: Small icebergs with surrounding brash ice can produce point-target signatures similar to vessels or offshore platforms.

classes.semantic_definition: Regions of sea surface with near-surface wind speed below the capillary wave generation threshold (< 2-3 m/s), resulting in specular reflection and very low radar backscatter.
classes.known_ambiguities: Major natural dark look-alike. Characterized by broad amorphous boundaries, wind-shadow alignment with coastal topography, and regional meteorological context.

classes.semantic_definition: Atmospheric boundary layer thermal convection producing open or closed honeycomb-like cloud/wind patterns, modulating radar backscatter into polygonal cellular networks.
classes.known_ambiguities: Weak open-cell convection centers can visually mimic diffuse biogenic slicks or low-wind patches.

classes.semantic_definition: Boundary between distinct upper-ocean water masses (temperature, salinity, or current velocity gradients), generating intense surface current convergence and wave-current interaction.
classes.known_ambiguities: Convergence lines frequently collect natural surfactants, forming co-located biogenic slicks.

classes.semantic_definition: Regular swell wave fields characterized by quasi-periodic spatial modulation of radar cross-section without significant atmospheric or slick disturbance.
classes.known_ambiguities: Short-crested swell under low wind can produce localized backscatter dips.

classes.semantic_definition: Precipitation features causing dual modulation: volume scattering and atmospheric attenuation from raindrops, combined with splash roughness and downdraft gust fronts at the ocean surface.
classes.known_ambiguities: Heavy rain downdrafts create bright rings surrounding dark rain-damped centers, which can be misclassified as slicks.

classes.semantic_definition: Continuous or fragmented frozen seawater (pack ice, grease ice, nilas, floes) covering the sea surface in polar and sub-polar seas.
classes.exclusion_reason: Domain-restricted polar phenomenon; grease ice and pancake ice create low backscatter similar to oil, but geographic domain is restricted to polar latitudes.
classes.known_ambiguities: Grease ice dampens capillary waves exactly like oil slicks, requiring temperature/latitude gating.

classes.semantic_definition: Quasi-parallel linear surface signatures aligned with the marine boundary layer wind vector, formed by atmospheric Langmuir circulation rolls modulating roughness.
classes.known_ambiguities: Linear streaks can resemble aligned biogenic slick filaments or trailing ship wakes.

classes.semantic_definition: Mesoscale or submesoscale rotating ocean vortices made visible on SAR imagery through spiral convergence filaments of natural surfactants or current-wave interaction.
classes.known_ambiguities: Spiral arms are comprised of concentrated biogenic slicks; boundary between Eddy and BS can be hierarchical.

classes.semantic_definition: Subsurface gravity waves propagating along oceanic pycnoclines, modulating surface roughness into characteristic alternating bright (convergence) and dark (divergence/slick) curved soliton bands.
classes.known_ambiguities: Divergence zones and surfactant-accumulating troughs form pronounced dark look-alike bands.

classes.semantic_definition: Man-made marine infrastructure and vessels, including ships, oil/gas production platforms, wind turbines, aquaculture cages, and coastal installations exhibiting strong metallic corner reflector backscatter.
classes.known_ambiguities: Vessels vs stationary platforms; point targets vs side-lobe cross artifacts. Strictly preserved as Artificial / Anthropogenic Objects; NEVER renamed to Vessel.

classes.semantic_definition: Anthropogenic petroleum hydrocarbon releases on the ocean surface.
classes.exclusion_reason: Deficient sample size (exactly 4 images, 1,702 pixels, 0.0005% of dataset). Explicitly noted by Li et al. as insufficient data for training. Must NEVER be used as an oil spill training class for OPS-01.
classes.known_ambiguities: High risk of degenerate overfitting; completely unrepresentative of petroleum spills.
